# CodexMeter 2.0.1
Follow-ups to the 2.0 notch, and the last two provider rings.
## What changed
### Token usage stays front and centre
2.0 moved the token accounting into Settings ▸ Usage, which risked burying the thing CodexMeter is *for*. This pulls it forward:
- The status-bar menu leads with **Token Usage…** (⌘U). - The notch's right-click menu has it too. - Reopening the app (Finder/Dock) opens the Usage view. - The Settings window opens on the Usage pane by default. - The notch tooltip shows today's local token total for Codex and Claude beside the limit rings — the "how much have I used" the ring's percentage doesn't give.
### Two more provider rings
- **Antigravity** — Gemini usage read from Antigravity's own local language server (the IDE or the `agy` CLI must be running; that is where the number lives). Google refuses a third-party client, so this is the door Antigravity itself uses. - The **Ollama Cloud** ring now works from a key pasted into **Settings ▸ Notch ▸ Ollama Cloud** (kept in the login Keychain), not only from `OLLAMA_API_KEY`.
### Cursor
When the Cursor editor has no session, the notch falls back to the `cursor-agent login` session.
## Fixed
- **The notch's provider polling ran even while the notch was hidden**, and a feedback loop (each fetch wrote its cache to `UserDefaults`, which `AccountLimitStore` reacted to) had it re-fetching every borrowed-credential provider several times a second. It now runs only while the notch is on screen, keyed on real limit changes. - The notch's right-click menu and a couple of settings strings still said "Codenotch". - The status-bar item now installs from `applicationWillFinishLaunching` too — a `Settings`-only app does not reliably reach `applicationDidFinishLaunching`.
## Verification
- 589 automated tests, 0 failures (9 environment-integration tests skipped). - `swift build` with zero warnings and zero errors. - Universal 2 build for Apple silicon and Intel Macs running macOS 14 or later. - Verified on a release build: hidden notch does no provider polling; the status item installs on launch. - Ad-hoc signed, not Apple-notarized. SHA-256 protects the first download; Sparkle authenticates later updates with Ed25519 signatures.
## Install or update with Homebrew
```bash brew update brew upgrade --cask --greedy dlfkdLR/tap/codexmeter ```
For a new installation:
```bash brew install --cask dlfkdLR/tap/codexmeter ```
```bash xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/CodexMeter.app open /Applications/CodexMeter.app ```
## First direct-download launch
Download `CodexMeter-2.0.1.dmg` and `SHA256SUMS.txt` into the same folder and verify the checksum before opening:
```bash cd ~/Downloads grep ' CodexMeter-2.0.1.dmg$' SHA256SUMS.txt | shasum -a 256 -c - open CodexMeter-2.0.1.dmg ```
Only after `OK`, copy `CodexMeter.app` to Applications and use the app-scoped quarantine command above.
## Recovery
This release does not migrate any database. Published version tags are immutable; corrections ship as a new patch release.
